+ CRL.M.C. 8475/2023, CRL.M.A. 31624/2023  DEEPAK KUMAR AND ORS. 
 Throug

versus  STATE OF NCT OF DELHI AND ANR. 
 Throug  
 
 CORAM:
 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SAURABH BANERJEE  ORDER % 12.12.2023 1.

The petitioners, vide the present petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973

, seek quashing of the FIR No.1093/2015 dated 15.09.2015 registered under Section(s)
498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and under Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act,
1961 at PS.: Shahbad Dairy, Outer District, Delhi and all proceeding emanating therefrom in view of the Settlement Agreement 20.09.2022 arrived at between the parties.
2. This petition is accompanied by the Settlement Agreement 20.09.2022 and is also supported by affidavits of all the petitioners and of respondent no.2, alongwith proofs of their respective I.Ds.
CRL.M.C. 8475/2023 page 1 of 3
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 14/12/2023 at 02:19:40 3.
Petitioner nos. 1 to 5 and as also respondent no.2 are present in Court and have been identified by the Investigating Officer.
Their credentials have been verified by this Court.
4. Issue Notice.
5. Learned APP accepts notice.
He confirms that he has no objection to the quashing of the FIR.
6. Learned counsel for the respondent no.2 also accepts notice.

Respondent no.2 confirms that the petitioner no.1 and respondent no.2 have been granted divorce by mutual consent vide Decree of Deepak Kumar And Ors vs State Of Nct Of Delhi And Anr on 12 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41286089/
1 Divorce dated 20.02.2023.

entities.text: Deepak Kumar And Ors vs State Of Nct Of Delhi And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: She further affirms the Settlement Agreement 20.09.2022 whereby the petitioner no.1 has already paid her a sum of Rs.40,000/- in full and final settlement of all her claims including alimony, maintenance (present, past and future), stridhan etc.
She states that she has no objection to the quashing of the present FIR.

7. In view of the settlement arrived at between the parties and following the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Jitendra Raghuvanshi & Ors. Vs. Babita Raguvanshi & Anr (2013) 4 SCC 58, Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab & Anr. (2012) 10 SCC 303 and Narinder Singh & Ors. vs. State of Punjab & Anr. (2014) 6 SCC 466, this Court is of the opinion that continuation of the aforesaid FIR will be an exercise in futility.

sentences.text: 8. Accordingly, the present petition is allowed and the FIR No.1093/2015 dated 15.09.2015 registered under Section(s) 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and under Section 4 of the Dowry CRL.M.C. 8475/2023 page 2 of 3
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 14/12/2023 at 02:19:40 Prohibition Act, 1961 at PS.: Shahbad Dairy, Outer District, Delhi and all proceeding emanating therefrom are quashed.

9. Needless to state that the settlement arrived at between the parties resulting in closure of all criminal proceedings inter se the parties by way of the present order will, in no way, effect the rights of the children of the petitioner no.1 and the respondent no.2 namely Master Dhruv vis-a-vis his parents, as may be available under law, in any manner whatsoever.
10. Accordingly, the present petition, alongwith the pending applications, if any, stands disposed of.
DECEMBER 12, 2023/So  CRL.M.C. 8475/2023
